small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_OC tiles (e.g. BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=128 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3) to the autotune list — OC=64 fits exactly in one tile of 64 but a 2D-balanced (M,N) GEMM tile usually wins; also try BLOCK_N=32/BLOCK_OC=64 to reduce register pressure from the 9-iter unrolled inner loop.
- The current kernel reloads the same x positions for every (oc tile) and recomputes 9 strided gathers per (ic) — switch to loading an x tile once into registers across the IC loop. Consider hoisting `b*stride_xb + oh*stride_xh + ow*stride_xw` and using a contiguous channels-last input view so the IC dimension becomes the GEMM-K and a single `tl.dot` can be issued per (kh,kw).
- Use `tl.dot` instead of explicit outer-product accumulation: stage x into [BLOCK_N, IC] and w into [IC, BLOCK_OC] for each (kh,kw), then `acc += tl.dot(x_tile, w_tile)`. With IC=8 (small), pad K to 16 in the tile and rely on Tensor Cores; this is the single biggest knob left.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM with channels-last (NHWC) input/output and weight laid out as [KH*KW*IC, OC]. Each program computes a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_OC] output tile using `tl.dot` over a K-loop of length `KH*KW*IC` (=72 here), gathering input rows on the fly. This turns the kernel into a real Tensor-Core GEMM instead of a vector-outer-product loop and should be 3-5× faster on this shape.
- Fuse the NCHW→NHWC permutation of the input into a small pre-kernel (or do it once and cache), and store output in NHWC then permute back; the conv kernel itself runs entirely on contiguous-channel data so the K-axis loads coalesce.
- Keep the hardswish∘relu fused in the epilogue exactly as now (closed form `x * clamp(x+3,0,6)/6` then max(·,0)), applied to the fp32 accumulator before the store. Use `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=3`, BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 as a starting tile.
